title: Deployment issues
content:
## Overview

Deployment issues fall into two broad categories: **build-time failures** (the agent cannot bundle or prepare your app) and **runtime failures** (your app starts but behaves incorrectly or crashes). This page walks through the most common scenarios and how to resolve them.

<Callout type="tip" title="Check the deployment pipeline first">
Most build errors appear in the **deployment pipeline log**. See [Deployment pipeline failures](/deployment-pipeline-failures) for step-by-step diagnostics.
</Callout>

---

## Build-time failures

### Missing dependencies

**Symptom:** Build fails with `Module not found` or `Cannot find package`.

**Cause:** The agent has not added a required library to `package.json` (Node.js), `requirements.txt` (Python), or your framework's manifest.

**Fix:**

<Steps>
<Step title="Identify the missing package">
Read the build log; the error message names the import that failed.
</Step>

<Step title="Tell the agent in chat">
"Install `[package-name]` and re‑deploy." The agent will add the dependency and trigger a new build.
</Step>

<Step title="Verify the manifest">
In the **Files** pane, confirm the package appears in `package.json` or `requirements.txt` before the next deployment.
</Step>
</Steps>

---

### Incompatible Node / Python version

**Symptom:** Build fails with syntax errors or a message like `Unexpected token` (Node) or `invalid syntax` (Python).

**Cause:** The deployment runtime uses a different language version than the code expects (for example, async/await syntax in Node 12, or Python 3.11 match statements on a Python 3.9 runtime).

**Fix:**

1. Check the [Deployment types](/deployment-types) page for the runtime version your plan provides.
2. Ask the agent: *"Use syntax compatible with Node 16"* (or the version you have).
3. Re‑generate the code and re‑deploy.

<Callout type="info">
If you need a specific runtime version, consider upgrading your [Deployment plan level](/deployment-plan-levels) or switching to a Docker‑based deployment (if available on your plan).
</Callout>

---

### Build timeout

**Symptom:** Build aborts with `Timeout exceeded` or `Build killed`.

**Cause:** The build step (install dependencies, transpile, bundle) runs longer than the time limit for your plan.

**Fix:**

<Tabs>
<Tab title="Reduce dependencies">
Ask the agent to remove unused libraries or combine smaller packages. Fewer dependencies = faster install.
</Tab>

<Tab title="Optimize build config">
For Next.js or Vite apps, disable source maps in production or switch to a lighter bundler mode. Example: *"Set `productionBrowserSourceMaps: false` in `next.config.js`."*
</Tab>

<Tab title="Upgrade plan">
Higher [Deployment plan levels](/deployment-plan-levels) offer longer build windows and more CPU.
</Tab>
</Tabs>

---

### Out of memory during build

**Symptom:** Build crashes with `JavaScript heap out of memory` or `Killed`.

**Cause:** The build process (Webpack, Vite, TypeScript compiler) exceeds available RAM.

**Fix:**

- **Node apps:** Add `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096` to your build environment (ask the agent to set this in the deployment config).
- **Simplify the build:** Split large bundles, enable tree‑shaking, or lazy‑load heavy modules.
- **Upgrade plan:** More RAM is available at higher tiers—see [Deployment plan levels](/deployment-plan-levels).

---

## Runtime failures

### App starts but shows a blank page

**Symptom:** Deployment succeeds; opening the URL displays a white screen or "Application error."

**Common causes & fixes:**

| Cause | How to diagnose | Fix |
|-------|-----------------|-----|
| Client‑side crash | Open browser DevTools → Console; look for uncaught exceptions. | Share the error with the agent: *"Fix runtime error: [paste stack trace]."* |
| Missing environment variable | App tries to read `process.env.API_KEY` but it's undefined. | Set the variable in the **Environment** pane and re‑deploy. See [How apps work here](/how-apps-work-here-mental-model#environment-variables). |
| Static‑asset 404 | CSS or JS files return 404; check Network tab in DevTools. | Ask the agent to fix the public path or output directory in the build config. |

---

### Database connection failures

**Symptom:** Logs show `MongoNetworkError`, `ECONNREFUSED`, or similar.

**Cause:** The app cannot reach the MongoDB instance—wrong connection string, firewall rule, or the database is not provisioned.

**Fix:**

<Steps>
<Step title="Verify the database is provisioned">
In the workspace sidebar, confirm a MongoDB database exists. If not, ask the agent: *"Add a MongoDB database to this project."*
</Step>

<Step title="Check the connection string">
The environment variable (usually `MONGODB_URI` or `DATABASE_URL`) must match the value shown in the **Environment** pane. Copy it exactly—include username, password, and database name.
</Step>

<Step title="Whitelist the deployment IP">
Some plans deploy from dynamic IPs. If your MongoDB host has an IP allowlist, add `0.0.0.0/0` (all IPs) or ask support for the deployment IP range.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Callout type="warning" title="Credentials in code">
Never hard‑code `mongodb://user:pass@host` in your source files. Always use environment variables and keep secrets out of version control.
</Callout>

Read more: [Database (MongoDB)](/database-mongodb).

---

### API or external service timeouts

**Symptom:** Requests to third‑party APIs (Stripe, OpenAI, etc.) hang or return `504 Gateway Timeout`.

**Possible causes:**

- **Rate limit:** Your API key has hit a quota.
- **Network policy:** The deployment environment blocks outbound HTTPS to certain domains (rare).
- **Slow endpoint:** The third‑party service is down or experiencing latency.

**Fix:**

1. **Check the third‑party status page** (e.g., `status.openai.com`).
2. **Increase timeout** in your HTTP client (Axios, Fetch): set `timeout: 30000` (30 seconds).
3. **Verify API key:** Confirm the key is valid and has sufficient quota; test it locally or in a tool like Postman.
4. **Review logs:** Look for `429 Too Many Requests` or `401 Unauthorized`—these point to credential or quota issues, not network problems.

---

### Deployment health check fails

**Symptom:** Deployment pipeline succeeds, but the platform marks the app as **unhealthy** and does not route traffic.

**Cause:** The health‑check endpoint (`/health` or `/`) does not return HTTP 200 within the timeout window.

**Fix:**

- **Add or fix the health route:** Ensure your app responds to `GET /health` (or the path configured in your deployment settings) with a 200 status and minimal logic (e.g., `res.json({ status: 'ok' })`).
- **Speed up startup:** Move heavy initialization (database seeding, large file reads) out of the main server bootstrap so the health check can succeed quickly.
- **Check the timeout setting:** Some plans allow you to configure the health‑check timeout—ask the agent to increase it if your app needs more time to warm up.

---

### Custom domain not resolving

**Symptom:** Visiting `app.yourdomain.com` shows a DNS error or "Site not found."

**Diagnosis:**

<Steps>
<Step title="Verify DNS records">
Run `dig app.yourdomain.com` or use an online DNS checker. The `CNAME` must point to the Emergent deployment hostname (shown in the **Custom domain** settings).
</Step>

<Step title="Wait for propagation">
DNS changes can take 1–48 hours to propagate globally. Test from multiple locations or use `8.8.8.8` as your resolver.
</Step>

<Step title="Check SSL certificate status">
In the workspace, navigate to **Custom domain** and confirm the SSL certificate is **Active**. If it shows **Pending**, wait a few more minutes; if **Failed**, double‑check the DNS `CNAME`.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Callout type="info">
Detailed setup instructions: [Custom domain](/custom-domain).
</Callout>

---

## Out of credits / quota exceeded

**Symptom:** Deployment is queued indefinitely or aborts with *"Insufficient credits."*

**Cause:** Your account has consumed its [credit allocation](/how-credits-work) for builds, compute time, or API calls.

**Fix:**

- **Check your balance:** Open the **Billing** or **Usage** dashboard (depending on your plan).
- **Upgrade or top up:** Purchase additional credits or move to a higher plan tier with more monthly allowance.
- **Optimize usage:** Reduce the number of deployments by batching changes; use preview builds sparingly.

---

## Image / video / audio generation failures

**Symptom:** AI‑generated media assets fail to appear or return errors.

**Cause:** Model unavailable, quota exceeded, or unsupported parameters.

**Fix:** See the dedicated page [AI media generation](/ai-media-generation-image-video-audio) for model‑specific troubleshooting and parameter guidance.

---

## Getting further help

If none of the above resolves your issue:

<CardGroup cols={2}>
<Card title="Ask the agent" icon="message-circle">
Paste the full error message into chat. The agent can read logs and often auto‑fix configuration mistakes.
</Card>

<Card title="Review the pipeline log" icon="list" href="/deployment-pipeline-failures">
Step‑by‑step guide to interpreting build and deploy logs.
</Card>

<Card title="Check platform status" icon="activity">
Rare outages or maintenance windows are announced on the Emergent status page (link in your workspace footer).
</Card>

<Card title="Contact support" icon="life-buoy">
Use the **Help** button in the workspace to open a ticket. Include your project ID and the timestamp of the failed deployment.
</Card>
</CardGroup>

<Callout type="success" title="Most issues resolve in chat">
The agent has access to your deployment logs and can iterate on fixes in real time—start there before opening a support ticket.
</Callout>
description: Common deployment failures and how to fix them.
